So I need to convey "recursion" visually. Classic visual metaphors for recursion:
- Fractals (Sierpinski triangle, tree branching)
- A spiral
- Nested boxes/shapes (like Russian dolls / matryoshka)
- The Droste effect (picture within a picture)
- A snake eating its tail (ouroboros) — more like loops though
- A tree where each branch splits into smaller branches — classic recursion
- Nested triangles (Sierpinski)

The key concept of recursion: a thing that contains/calls itself; self-similarity; a function calling itself; breaking a problem into smaller versions of the same problem.

A fractal tree is a strong visual: each branch produces smaller copies of itself. Nested squares/triangles also convey self-similarity. A Sierpinski triangle is very recognizable as a fractal — recursive structure.
